free.municipal: A municipal charger. Public chargers that municipalities built with EU funds are free for their first 5 years; this is likely one.
free.powerPlant: On the grounds of a {owner} power plant. Most likely for staff and visitors, hence free; outsiders may not get in.
free.airport: An airport charger. {owner} is building charging airside for buses and service cars, so this one is most likely not public.
free.fleet: Owned by the transport company {owner}. Most likely for its own fleet, hence free; it may not be open to others.
free.workplace: Owned by {owner}, which pays for the electricity itself. Probably for staff or customers; access may be limited.
free.networkPaid: Other chargers on this network are paid, so “free” here may be a register error.
free.unknown: The register says charging is free but gives no reason. It may be a promotion or limited access.
